# 🔍 Side Project — Analysis

## The Problem

Managing a personal side project in a generic note-taking app means the braindump, the plan, the architecture decisions, and the task list live in four different places with no connective tissue. By the time the project revives after a week away, reconstructing context takes longer than the actual work session. The core pain is context reconstruction overhead, not lack of planning discipline.

## Hard Constraints

- Solo project — no team features, no multi-user, no real-time collaboration.
- Must run locally; no cloud infrastructure costs for a side project budget.
- Total build time budget is 2 weekends (roughly 16 hours).
- Tech stack must be something already known — no learning curve budget here.

## Open Questions

- **Storage format**: SQLite vs. flat Markdown files? Options: (a) SQLite for queryability, (b) Markdown files in a git repo for version history, (c) hybrid (metadata in SQLite, content in Markdown).
- **AI integration**: Use the local Ollama model for spec generation or defer AI features entirely? Options: (a) Ollama now, (b) cloud API with a usage cap, (c) no AI — manual templates only.
- **Distribution**: Electron desktop app, local web server, or CLI? Options: (a) Electron (native feel, harder build), (b) local web server on `localhost:3000`, (c) pure CLI.

## Dependencies & Sequencing

- The storage decision must be made first — it is the lowest layer and every other component depends on it.
- The AI integration decision gates the spec generation feature — if deferred, manual templates must be designed as the primary path.
- Distribution format gates the UI framework choice — Electron permits React, a local web server is framework-agnostic, CLI is Node.js with Ink or plain stdout.

## Explicitly Out of Scope

- **Collaboration**: A solo project tool that adds collaboration is a different product — the mental model shifts from personal context to team coordination.
- **Mobile app**: Desktop / local-first, not mobile-first; mobile access deferred indefinitely.
- **Cloud sync**: Adds complexity (auth, conflict resolution, storage costs) disproportionate to the solo use case for this project.

# 🎯 Epic: Side Project — Personal Spec Manager

## Business Value

This is a personal productivity tool, so "business value" translates to personal leverage: reducing context-reconstruction time before each work session from ~20 minutes to under 2 minutes. The secondary value is that it replaces four disconnected tools (notes app, Notion, GitHub issues, and a scratchpad file) with a single local artefact that travels with the project.

The tertiary value is meta: building this tool with a structured spec pipeline validates the spec-first workflow on a small, low-stakes project before using it for larger work. It is its own proof of concept.

## Scope

### What This Epic Covers

- Local web server (Node.js, `localhost:3000`) serving a single-page dashboard
- Project creation from a braindump text input
- Spec generation via Ollama (local LLM) — analysis, epic, architecture
- Markdown file storage in a per-project directory
- Simple file browser to navigate generated specs

### What This Epic Does NOT Cover

- ❌ Multi-user or collaboration — solo tool
- ❌ Cloud sync — local-first only
- ❌ Mobile — desktop browser only
- ❌ Version history UI — files are in a git repo; use `git log` for history

## Tasks

| # | Task | Dependencies | Parallel | Effort | Priority |
|---|------|--------------|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | **Storage layer (Markdown files + index JSON)** | None | — | 2 hrs | High |
| 2 | **Ollama spec generation chain** | Task 1 | — | 4 hrs | High |
| 3 | **Local web server + file browser UI** | Task 1 | Task 2 | 6 hrs | High |
| 4 | **Braindump → spec pipeline wiring** | Task 2, Task 3 | — | 2 hrs | High |
| 5 | **Polish: search, keyboard shortcuts, dark mode** | Task 4 | — | 2 hrs | Low |

## Success Criteria

- ✅ Can open any stored project and read its spec files in under 10 seconds
- ✅ New project spec generated from a braindump in under 3 minutes (Ollama speed)
- ✅ All spec files stored as plain Markdown — readable without the tool
- ✅ Zero external API calls — fully offline capable

- [Analysis](./analysis.md) — Problems driving this epic
- [Solution Architecture](./architecture.md) — System design
- [Timeline](./timeline.md) — Status tracking

# 🏗️ Solution Architecture: Side Project — Personal Spec Manager

## Architecture Overview

The simplest possible architecture that solves the context-reconstruction problem: a Node.js Express server running locally, reading and writing Markdown files from a `~/specs/` directory. No database, no auth, no deployment — just a file server with a web UI and a local LLM call.

The stack is deliberately boring. Express handles routing. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS (no framework build step) keeps the UI layer zero-dependency and instantly bootable. Ollama runs as a separate local process; the server calls its REST API at `localhost:11434`. The only state is the filesystem.

This architecture is intentionally not extensible. It solves one problem for one person. Any generalisation (multi-user, sync, mobile) would require a complete redesign — that is fine, because this is not a product, it is a personal tool.

## Design Principles

| Principle | Application |
|-----------|-------------|
| Filesystem as database | Each project is a directory; each spec is a `.md` file; no ORM, no migrations |
| Zero build step | The web UI is plain HTML + CSS + vanilla JS served directly — no bundler |
| Local LLM only | Ollama at `localhost:11434`; no API keys, no cloud costs, works offline |
| Boring is fast | Express + Node.js = 0 minutes of framework overhead on a Saturday afternoon |

## Component Design

### File Storage
**Purpose**: Projects stored at `~/specs/{project-slug}/`. Each directory contains `braindump.md`, `analysis.md`, `epic.md`, `architecture.md`. An `index.json` at `~/specs/index.json` holds project metadata (name, slug, created-at) for fast project listing without reading every directory.

### Ollama Chain
**Purpose**: Three sequential POST requests to `localhost:11434/api/generate` using `llama3` (or whatever model is pulled). Analysis → Epic → Architecture. Results written to the filesystem immediately after each step — if the server crashes mid-chain, partial results are preserved.

### Express API
**Purpose**: Four routes: `GET /api/projects` (list from index.json), `GET /api/projects/:slug/files/:filename` (read a spec file), `POST /api/projects` (create project + trigger chain), `GET /api/projects/:slug/status` (poll generation status via a simple in-memory flag).

### Web UI
**Purpose**: Single HTML file served at `/`. JavaScript fetches the project list on load, renders a sidebar, and displays the active spec file as rendered Markdown via `marked.js` loaded from a CDN. No framework, no build step.

## Technology Stack

| Layer | Choice | Rationale |
|-------|--------|-----------|
| Runtime | Node.js 20 LTS | Already installed; no new tools |
| Web framework | Express 4 | Minimal; two hours to a working server |
| UI | Vanilla HTML/JS + marked.js (CDN) | Zero build step; instantly editable |
| LLM | Ollama (`llama3`) | Local; no API key; works offline |
| Storage | Markdown files + `index.json` | Human-readable; git-versionable; no migration |

## Design Decisions

| Decision | Rationale | Trade-offs |
|----------|-----------|------------|
| Plain files over SQLite | Files are human-readable and git-friendly without tooling | No joins, no full-text search — acceptable for a solo tool with < 100 projects |
| No framework for UI | Zero build step means the server is running in 30 seconds | No component reuse, no TypeScript — acceptable for a UI this simple |
| Sequential chain (not parallel) | Ollama on a laptop is single-threaded in practice; parallel calls cause quality regression | Slower total time (~3 min vs. ~1 min) — acceptable for a background operation |
| In-memory status flag | Simplest polling mechanism; server restart clears it | If the server restarts mid-chain, the client sees stale status — fix by checking file existence |
